newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth says Ga. delays long-distance plan.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth says Ga. delays long-distance plan.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said Friday the Georgia Public Service Commission rejected a portion of its application to offer long-distance telephone service to customers in the state.

Lynn Bress, spokeswoman for BellSouth in Georgia, said the company would wait to receive the commission's order in writing before asking the panel to reconsider its decision, which came in a 5-0 vote on Thursday.
The order was expected to arrive next week.
The portion rejected by the PSC involved a statement of general terms and conditions for interconnection with competitors in local service markets.

The PSC also rejected interconnection and resale rates contained in the application and said it felt BellSouth's electronic interfaces were not at a standard necessary for a competitive environment, the company said.
Those issues were preliminary to a 14-point check list outlining BellSouth's plan for offering long-distance services, on which the PSC did not rule.
The PSC also did not take up the question of whether BellSouth's presence in the long-distance business would be in the public interest.
"We're just confused by their decision," said Bress.

"We already have 45 interconnection agreements in place in Georgia that the PSC approved and even sanctioned the rates. Yet yesterday, they rejected it. The terms and conditions were a mirror image," she said. "Also, they rejected the portion about electronic interfaces. But today, as we speak, we're flowing orders for competitors."
